notes: Scoping confirmed empirically, matching what the contract's own guidance already claims: despite the path param being project_id, the response is GROUP-scoped, not project-scoped - it returned all 12 active users of group 2615 (same set/shape as the sibling capability list_group_users, which takes no project id at all, and as list_users which also requires project_id but doesn't filter by it). project_id 379335744 only had to be a project the caller can see; nothing in the response ties back to that project. This is the third user-listing capability with this pattern (alongside list_users and list_group_users) - the routing eval's difficulty telling them apart is well-founded since all three return the identical group-wide user set from a project-scoped-looking path/params. users list was non-empty (12 rows) so the item shape and myself shape were both verifiable, not an empty-case UNVERIFIED situation. Declared 200 schema (success, users[], myself, info) matched the actual response exactly in both directions - no declared_missing, no undeclared_returned. Only the default query (no q, no p) was exercised; the q/q[email]/q[id]/p variants described in the contract were not separately probed since the base contract shape was already fully confirmed by the default call and further variants would be redundant for a PASS verdict.
